title: T1496 — Resource Hijacking
subtitle: This simulation shows a complete resource hijacking attack on a small cloud company.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: Scanning
steps.caption: The attacker probes internet-facing services and finds an old web application with a known, unpatched flaw. The firewall sees ordinary scan noise, so no alert fires
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Entry
steps.caption: The attacker sends the exploit and the application runs it. A web shell (a hidden script that passes attacker commands through the web app) gives them command execution on the server. The attacker and the company now share the same server, without the company knowing

steps.title: Downloading the miner
steps.caption: The attacker uses the web shell to download a cryptocurrency miner, renames it to look like a system tool, and starts it. The binary lands in a temporary folder, a place normal software rarely uses
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Connecting to the pool
steps.caption: The miner opens a long-lived connection to a mining pool (a server that groups miners and pays them for their work) and starts hashing (doing the miner's arithmetic work). CPU use jumps to about 95% and stays there. The pool now sends mining jobs; the server sends back completed work called shares
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Looking like normal load
steps.caption: The attacker throttles CPU to look like ordinary load and routes pool traffic over a port normally used for HTTPS. Cloud logs show nothing unusual yet

steps.title: Defender signals
steps.caption: The SOC sees three signals together: a process named like a system tool running from a temp folder, sustained CPU above baseline, and a 12-hour outbound session to a suspicious host. Correlation raises one high-severity alert
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Response
steps.caption: The SOC isolates the server from the network, kills the miner, and removes the web shell. The mining pool connection drops and CPU returns to normal within minutes
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.
